description: Curated 'worth a look' country sets for /countries, keyed by Ember region plus a world default.
why: The obvious way to build this list was to rank countries by the score the fact
engine already gives each hero fact. That does not work: the score is normalised
within each family against that family's 95th percentile, so its job is 'is this
fact publishable', not 'is this country more interesting than that one'. 82 of
200 countries sit at exactly 1.0 and the ties fall out alphabetically. Sorting by
it would produce Aruba, Afghanistan, Albania, Armenia - an alphabetical list
wearing a ranking's clothes.
So this is editorial, in the same spirit as blocs.json and geothermal-grids.json:
a person picked them. The bar is that a reader who knows nothing about
electricity should be surprised by the claim, and that the six in a set should
surprise them in six different ways rather than six variations of 'runs on oil'.
Selection only, no copy. Each card renders the country's own hero headline from
country-facts.json, which is already numeral-audited and regenerates on a data
refresh. A hand-written line here would be a third place for the same claim to
go stale, and question-insights.json is enough of that already.
North America has no set on purpose. Only 4 of its countries have a page - the
same reason CLAUDE.md gives for it having no regional ranking - and 'grids worth
a look near you' drawn from four, one of which is the reader's own, is not a
recommendation. Those visitors get the world set, which is the better answer.
check-data.js fails the build if any code here has no page.
